Sarrona: This short blade is printed from drake bone. Its gentle curve
column3: ground thin
column4: gives it the outline of a long fang
column5: which is how the Dragon Fang Dagger acquired its name. Deep red material wraps the handle and keeps the grip secure. Polishing gradually reveals the layers in the bone blade. On a sufficiently pure example
column6: the fine patterns remain clear even after getting wet and being wiped dry.

name: print_katana_name

name: print_katana_desc
Sarrona: A long blade made from drake bone and Sulfur Fire
column3: usable as a cutting tool. Its length calls for extra storage space
column4: while the purity of the bone determines its value.

name: print_katana_flavor
Sarrona: The long
column3: pale blade has a gentle curve
column4: with warm red markings left by Sulfur Fire during processing. The lines grow finer toward the cutting edge. Though the blade has cooled completely
column5: the red remains as distinct as when it first left the furnace. Drake bone gives a blade of this length considerable resilience. Put it away and it is easy to see just how much more space it needs than an ordinary short knife.

name: print_katana_recipe
Sarrona: Prints a katana from drake bone and Sulfur Fire. The bone material affects the blade's finish and value.

Sarrona: A two-handed drake-bone greatsword with a broad
column3: thick blade that takes up considerable space. It can serve as a cutting tool

name: print_greatsword_flavor
Sarrona: A broad
column3: thick bone blade joins a deep red guard
column4: with a handle long enough for both hands. Lift it and the amount of bone used becomes apparent. Layers in the bone remain visible along the blade
column5: running down toward the guard. A piece this large uses plenty of material and takes some time to print. By the time it is finally ready

name: print_fire_smg_flavor

column3: with the metal receiver visible through the seams. The original markings remain on the outside
column4: while fine grooves have been pressed into the grip. It feels solid and substantial in the hand. The metal inside deserves as much care as the scale casing. Better metal produces a weapon that runs more smoothly.

name: bone_brick_medium_flavor
Sarrona: Loose drake bone fragments are smelted and pressed into these gray-white bricks
column3: leaving no trace of their original shapes as fish or rat bones. Small pores remain on the surface

name: bone_brick_high_desc
Sarrona: Flux has removed much of the impurity from this bone brick. It produces more effective attachments and more valuable blades.

name: bone_brick_high_flavor
Sarrona: Flux helps separate impurities from the fragments during smelting
column3: giving the cooled brick a more even color and a much finer grain across its broken face. Lightly polish away the rough outer layer and faint patterns from the original bone become visible. They sometimes survive on the surface of a printed item too. Turn it in the light and it looks rather like naturally carved bone.

name: bone_brick_extreme_desc
Sarrona: Refining with Sulfur Fire leaves purer bone material
column3: suitable for more effective attachments and finer blades. When used for ammunition
column4: it also yields more finished rounds.

name: bone_brick_extreme_flavor
Sarrona: Refining with Sulfur Fire gives the brick a cleaner color
column3: with pale violet markings beneath its bone-white surface. Even when cool
column4: a faint trace of sulfur can still be detected near a broken face. Very few impurities remain in the material. When printed into fine attachments
column5: it more readily retains the natural resilience and strength of drake bone.

name: print_spring_chip_flavor
Sarrona: A line bends back and forth across the face
column3: outlining the little set of springs. The stored design carefully accounts for even the smallest joints
column4: including where the bone material and metal meet. The finished parts are small
column5: though printing them takes time. They will have to move repeatedly
column6: after all
column7: and a rough detail can affect the performance of the whole set.

name: print_sight_chip_flavor
Sarrona: A red dot sits inside a thin ring. It is a simple design
column3: with no manufacturer's mark along the edge. Inside is the complete pattern for the bone frame and base
column4: with the placement of the printing plastic already worked out. Put this unassuming little chip in the printer and it can turn a bone brick into a slender sight.

name: print_silencer_chip_flavor
Sarrona: A short
column3: dark tube is printed on the face
column4: crossed by two red lines that match the overlapping plates on the finished piece. The layers recorded in the design are much more complex than this small picture suggests. Bone material and metal must be brought together gradually during printing to form the complete tube. For something so short
column5: a fair amount of work goes into it.

name: print_magazine_chip_flavor
Sarrona: Two teal blocks
column3: one higher than the other
column4: are printed on the face without any explanation beside them. The complete magazine design only appears once the chip is in the printer. Inside the narrow shell
column5: the design also accounts for loading and feeding ammunition
column6: so printing takes time even with all the materials ready. The finished piece looks much longer than the little block on the chip.

name: print_dagger_chip_flavor
Sarrona: The face bears the outline of a short blade
column3: its spine slightly curved
column4: with a small patch of deep red at the handle. The design keeps the fang-like curve
column5: while the bone's own patterns remain on the blade after printing. Even when the same chip is used every time
column6: a different bone brick leaves small differences in the finished dagger.

name: print_katana_chip_flavor

column3: with a little orange beside the handle
column4: as though the finished sword's warm red markings have been shrunk into the picture too. The stored design lays out the processing of bone material and Sulfur Fire along the whole blade
column5: preserving even its gentle curve. The chip is only a small piece in the hand. The sword it prints needs a much longer space.

name: print_greatsword_chip_flavor
Sarrona: The broad blade and guard take up most of the face

column5: making it a lengthy job. There is no way to tell where that scale once grew. By the time the finished weapon comes out

name: manual_dairy_note_2_title
Sarrona: A bottle of dragon milk wine

name: manual_dairy_note_2_section_1
Sarrona: Filling the bottle

name: manual_dairy_note_2_body_1
Sarrona: Pour one pouch of milk into the wine bottle and add 250 mL of water. Put one vial of dragon saliva in the ingredient slots. For a richer wine use 750 mL of milk. Concentrated milk counts by its volume before evaporation. Top it up with water to fill the bottle.

name: manual_dairy_note_2_section_2
Sarrona: Young wine and aged wine

name: manual_dairy_note_2_body_2
Sarrona: Leave it overnight. A pouch with base water makes Homebrew. High-quality water gives Production Wine and pure water gives Reserve. A full bottle of undiluted milk makes Master Vintage. Either wine gains 3% of its starting base value each night for twenty nights.

name: manual_dairy_note_3_title
Sarrona: Once the pouch is open

name: manual_dairy_note_3_section_1
Sarrona: Have a pitcher ready

name: manual_dairy_note_3_body_1
Sarrona: Each pouch holds 500 mL and must be emptied at once. Pour it into a large enough vessel before measuring smaller amounts. Feeding Sarrona grants milk at 5
column3: 000 nutrition and every 10
column4: 000 thereafter
column5: in a container chosen by her nutrition after feeding. This milk is already opened.

name: manual_dairy_note_3_section_2
Sarrona: Refrigerating opened milk

name: manual_dairy_note_3_body_2
Sarrona: Dragon milk is so rich in nutrients that it spoils readily when exposed to air. Refrigerate the milk after opening. The cold slows spoilage
column3: although it cannot prevent it altogether.

name: manual_dairy_note_3_section_3
Sarrona: Storage life

name: manual_dairy_note_3_body_3
Sarrona: Opened milk turns to organic waste overnight at room temperature. Even in a powered refrigerator it keeps for at most four days. If fresh milk is added to an older batch
column3: count from the day the oldest pouch was opened.

name: manual_dairy_note_4_title
Sarrona: Fresh milk in water

name: manual_dairy_note_4_section_1
Sarrona: A little milk for the counter

name: manual_dairy_note_4_body_1
Sarrona: Measure 20 mL of fresh milk and top up with water to make one litre. Label the bottle for what it contains. Some customers who buy a single bottle to drink themselves may return for another.

name: manual_dairy_note_4_section_2
Sarrona: A little milk for the plants

name: manual_dairy_note_4_body_2
Sarrona: For plants
column3: 5 mL of fresh milk per finished litre is enough to help. At 10 and 20 mL the seedlings grow faster
column4: the harvest is larger and the produce is finer. Use the mixture while the milk is fresh.

name: manual_dairy_note_5_title
Sarrona: Dragon milk nutrient tablets

name: manual_dairy_note_5_section_1
Sarrona: Making and using the tablets

name: manual_dairy_note_5_body_1
Sarrona: Heat the milk to at least 100°C to sterilize it
column3: then place it in the evaporator. Once the milk has dried to a powder
column4: press it into nutrient tablets. Dissolve one tablet per five litres of water to improve plant growth and yield.

name: manual_dairy_note_5_section_2
Sarrona: Heating and drying

name: manual_dairy_note_5_body_2
Sarrona: Fit a chemical module to the standard heating plate so it can sterilize the milk. After one night in a standard evaporator a 500 mL pouch leaves concentrated milk in the bottle. After the second night 200 mL of powder settles at the bottom.

name: manual_dairy_note_5_section_3
Sarrona: Pressing and storage

name: manual_dairy_note_5_body_3
Sarrona: Select Dragon Milk Nutrient Tablet on the Chem Finisher. Each 100 mL of powder makes five tablets. One pouch yields 200 mL of powder and makes ten tablets in two batches. Impurities carry over
column3: so use clean ingredients. One tablet in 5 L gives 50% faster growth and 30% more yield; in 10 L
column4: half as much. The dissolved plant feed keeps.

name: manual_dairy_note_8_title
Sarrona: Ripening and storing dragon cheese

name: manual_dairy_note_8_section_1
Sarrona: Setting and pressing the curds

name: manual_dairy_note_8_body_1
Sarrona: Sterilize two pouches of pure milk or enough pure concentrate to equal 1 L of fresh milk. Add one vial of dragon saliva. Cut the curds with a blade and wrap them in Kotton fabric to drain and press two wheels. Keep the fabric for the next batch.

name: manual_dairy_note_8_section_2
Sarrona: Ripening time

name: manual_dairy_note_8_body_2
Sarrona: Freshly pressed cheese can already be eaten. At room temperature it reaches the aged stage after four days and becomes fully ripe at eight. Only then will buyers take it as a luxury. Once fully ripe
column3: it spoils if left at room temperature for another night. A powered standard AgeWell roughly halves the wait. Before the wheel is fully ripe
column4: chilling pauses ripening until it is taken out.

name: manual_dairy_note_8_section_3
Sarrona: Storing ripe cheese

name: manual_dairy_note_8_body_3
Sarrona: Keep ripe dragon cheese in the refrigerator
column3: as a second fermentation can easily spoil it. Although the cheese becomes more nourishing
column4: the flavour changes and a coating of mould makes it far less appealing. Few customers will try it
column5: which makes it difficult to sell.

name: manual_dairy_note_10_title
Sarrona: Keeping the scent of dragon saliva

name: manual_dairy_note_10_section_1
Sarrona: Drawing off the water

name: manual_dairy_note_10_body_1
Sarrona: The saliva in the vial is already diluted. Dissolve one vial in an empty vessel and place it in a powered evaporator. Once the water is gone
column3: 10 mL of aromatic extract will remain
column4: enough for one dose of ambergris.

name: manual_dairy_note_10_section_2
Sarrona: Scent for the shop

name: manual_dairy_note_10_body_2
Sarrona: Place the dry extract in the Chem Finisher and select Dragon Ambergris. Use a dose before opening the shop and customers will pay 10% more that day. By the following day this effect has worn off.

name: manual_husbandry_note_2_title
Sarrona: The first milk feed

name: manual_husbandry_note_2_section_1
Sarrona: Mixing the feed

name: manual_husbandry_note_2_body_1
Sarrona: Fit the dispenser to the cage and blend a milk pouch with the rats’ usual food. If a pouch is already open
column3: pick up the vessel and click a hungry rat you own. It drinks as much as it needs.

name: manual_husbandry_note_2_section_2
Sarrona: What the rat actually eats

name: manual_husbandry_note_2_body_2
Sarrona: Rats and fish recover some health that night if milk supplies at least 5% of the calories they actually eat. Every two such nights raise constitution by one level up to level five. Nights on ordinary feed preserve the progress already made. Each level adds 10% to a rat’s base weight limit for a total of 50% at level five.

name: manual_husbandry_note_4_title
Sarrona: Feed and water for the tank

name: manual_husbandry_note_4_section_1
Sarrona: Where the feed goes

name: manual_husbandry_note_4_body_1
Sarrona: Power the system and fit a filled water tank and a filter before adding fish. Place a whole milk pouch in the tank inventory for fish to eat or mix it into food in the dispenser. Meat and milk suit sturgeon and both kinds of eel. Milk poured into the water does not count as feed.

name: manual_husbandry_note_4_section_2
Sarrona: Before leaving the tank overnight

name: manual_husbandry_note_4_body_2
Sarrona: A tankful that once lasted the night may run short as the fish grow. At level five
column3: a milk-fed fish needs 50% more water as an ordinary one of the same size. Check water
column4: feed and organic waste before nightfall.

name: manual_husbandry_note_6_title
Sarrona: Raising the next generation

name: manual_husbandry_note_6_section_1
Sarrona: What a pup inherits

name: manual_husbandry_note_6_body_1
Sarrona: Give an adult pair food and space for pups. Ordinary rats breed as usual. Higher milk levels reduce fertility. At conception
column3: pups inherit the parents’ average level
column4: rounded down. A level-five rat paired with an ordinary one gives level-two pups.

name: manual_husbandry_note_6_section_2
Sarrona: Leave the roe in the tank

name: manual_husbandry_note_6_body_2
Sarrona: Keep a fed adult tilapia pair of the same species together. Leave the roe for fertilization and six fry will hatch. Fry inherit the parents’ average level
column3: rounded down. Higher-level females lay less often. Eels and sturgeon do not breed in tanks.

name: manual_husbandry_note_8_title
Sarrona: What the stock yields

name: manual_husbandry_note_8_section_1
Sarrona: Bone fragments alongside the meat

name: manual_husbandry_note_8_body_1
Sarrona: Butchering an adult rat or fish at level two or higher gives one bone fragment per 500 g of body weight. Round any remainder up. Inherited levels count. Fish also yield 10% more of their base meat per level for a total of 50% more at level five.

name: manual_husbandry_note_8_section_2
Sarrona: Skin grafts and electricity

name: manual_husbandry_note_8_body_2
Sarrona: Raise graft tilapia for patches. At level five
column3: each 150 grams of body weight yields one patch. Once an electric eel reaches its generating stage
column4: levels one and two add one charge nightly
column5: three and four add two
column6: and level five adds three.

name: manual_husbandry_note_8_section_3
Sarrona: Roe from sturgeon

name: manual_husbandry_note_8_body_3
Sarrona: Raise sturgeon for roe. Each milk level adds four grams per growth cycle
column3: reaching sixty grams at level five. A sturgeon can carry roe up to fifteen percent of its body weight
column4: so a larger fish has more room for it.

name: manual_forge_note_2_title
Sarrona: What a dragon scale yields

name: manual_forge_note_2_section_1
Sarrona: Smelting a scale

name: manual_forge_note_2_body_1
Sarrona: One scale from Sarrona is enough for a firing. Fit a charged power source
column3: put the scale in the intake and clear the output. A scale fired alone yields one portion each of Dragon Scale Powder and Sulfur Fire overnight. Use the powder in a filter or take it to ease tobacco
column4: alcohol and narcotic withdrawal. For a Sentinel
column5: each dose takes 3 days off the injection counter.

name: manual_forge_note_2_section_2
Sarrona: Adding flux

name: manual_forge_note_2_body_2
Sarrona: Place flux beside the scale to collect one portion of powder and two portions of Sulfur Fire by morning. Basic flux is spent
column3: while advanced flux can be used again. Keep the fire for dragon breath rounds or the purest bone bricks.

name: manual_forge_note_4_title
Sarrona: Three grades from the same bones

name: manual_forge_note_4_section_1
Sarrona: Medium and high purity

name: manual_forge_note_4_body_1
Sarrona: Two fragments fired alone make one medium-purity brick. For a higher grade
column3: add one basic flux
column4: or use advanced flux if you have it. Either gives a high-purity brick overnight.

name: manual_forge_note_4_section_2
Sarrona: The highest grade

name: manual_forge_note_4_body_2
Sarrona: Pair two fragments with one sulfur fire for the highest grade. There is no need to add flux as well. If scales share the intake with a pair of fragments
column3: the furnace processes the bone brick first and leaves the scales for later.

name: manual_forge_note_6_title
Sarrona: Saving up for a batch

name: manual_forge_note_6_section_1
Sarrona: Allow for each brick

name: manual_forge_note_6_body_1
Sarrona: Sarrona sometimes brings a batch chip. Fit it to the furnace to make up to three bricks of one grade overnight. A full batch takes six fragments. For high purity add three basic flux or share one advanced flux across the batch. For the highest grade allow three sulfur fire.

name: manual_forge_note_6_section_2
Sarrona: When to take the chip out

name: manual_forge_note_6_body_2
Sarrona: A standard furnace draws twenty charge per cycle with the chip fitted
column3: up from eight. The same cost applies to a single brick or a scale. Remove the chip for smaller jobs
column4: and leave enough output space for the whole batch.

name: manual_forge_note_8_title
Sarrona: Drawing water through the filter

name: manual_forge_note_8_section_1
Sarrona: Upgrading a used cartridge

name: manual_forge_note_8_body_1
Sarrona: Drag one portion of powder onto your basic or advanced cartridge. Its remaining durability carries over
column3: up to 300 for either grade. Leave it fitted overnight to recover 10 durability on the basic version or 60 on the advanced one.

name: manual_forge_note_8_section_2
Sarrona: What passes through

name: manual_forge_note_8_body_2
Sarrona: Fit a working cartridge in a three-litre filter pitcher
column3: then pour liquid in or draw from a water source. Fish systems use it too. It removes heavy metals and chemical contaminants. Minerals
column4: poisons
column5: dream cap extract and dragon milk pass through.

name: manual_forge_note_8_section_3
Sarrona: When microbes are present

name: manual_forge_note_8_body_3
Sarrona: When microbes are present
column3: the trapped contaminants turn into organic waste. With water and waste available
column4: the microbes can multiply. In water without microbes the trapped contaminants disappear
column5: leaving no new organic waste.

name: manual_print_note_2_title
Sarrona: Before a print run

name: manual_print_note_2_section_1
Sarrona: Chips and power

name: manual_print_note_2_body_1
Sarrona: Sarrona’s selection varies from visit to visit. Each printer chip holds one pattern. Power the printer
column3: fit the Metal Printing Module and insert the matching chip. Take it back when the job is done and use it for the next batch.

name: manual_print_note_2_section_2
Sarrona: Choosing the bricks

name: manual_print_note_2_body_2
Sarrona: Brick purity carries into the finished piece. Small fittings take just one brick of any grade. For a katana or greatsword
column3: gather matching bricks and clear room in the output tray before starting.

name: manual_print_note_4_title
Sarrona: Loose Dragon Breath rounds

name: manual_print_note_4_section_1
Sarrona: What a brick yields

name: manual_print_note_4_body_1
Sarrona: One brick and one Sulfur Fire go into a run with the Dragon Breath chip. At standard speed it takes two nights. A medium brick gives six loose rounds, a high brick eight and a purple-veined extreme brick thirteen.

name: manual_print_note_4_section_2
Sarrona: Making room in the tray

name: manual_print_note_4_body_2
Sarrona: Loose rounds drop into the tray one at a time. If it fills halfway through the batch
column3: collect what is already there. The printer can release the rest on its next cycle without another set of ingredients.

name: manual_print_note_6_title
Sarrona: Materials for small prints

name: manual_print_note_6_section_1
Sarrona: A brick and an ingot

name: manual_print_note_6_body_1
Sarrona: The precision spring
column3: fang dagger and suppressor each take one brick and one metal ingot. Choose the chip for the piece you want. At standard speed the spring and dagger take two nights
column4: the suppressor three.

name: manual_print_note_6_section_2
Sarrona: A brick and a spool

name: manual_print_note_6_body_2
Sarrona: Both the sight and the extended magazine need a brick and a spool of printing plastic. Check the chip face for a red-centred ring or two teal squares respectively. Either pattern takes two nights at standard speed.

name: manual_print_note_9_title
Sarrona: Room for longer pieces

name: manual_print_note_9_section_1
Sarrona: Fire Dragon Katana

name: manual_print_note_9_body_1
Sarrona: Choose two matching bricks and one Sulfur Fire for the katana chip. Clear a strip nine cells long in the output tray. A standard printer takes three nights to finish the blade.

name: manual_print_note_9_section_2
Sarrona: Red Dragon Greatsword

name: manual_print_note_9_body_2
Sarrona: The greatsword chip calls for four matching bricks and two Sulfur Fire. The piece is nine cells long like the katana
column3: but two cells wide. Leave that space clear for collection after five nights at standard speed.

name: manual_print_note_11_title
Sarrona: Grading the Fire Dragon Lin

name: manual_print_note_11_section_1
Sarrona: Keeping a whole scale

name: manual_print_note_11_body_1
Sarrona: Keep one whole dragon scale for this pattern. With the Fire Dragon Lin chip fitted
column3: the printer takes the scale
column4: a metal ingot and one Sulfur Fire. At standard speed the print is ready in five nights.

name: manual_print_note_11_section_2
Sarrona: Reading the ingot grade

name: manual_print_note_11_body_2
Sarrona: The ingot determines the result. A fair or lower ingot gives a medium print
column3: and a high ingot gives a high one. Very high ingots give extreme prints. Only a perfect ingot makes a perfect Fire Dragon Lin.

name: manual_dairy_note_11_title
Sarrona: Drinking Dragon Milk and Using Ambergris

name: manual_dairy_note_11_section_1
Sarrona: Drinking from the pouch

name: manual_dairy_note_11_body_1
Sarrona: Drinking a pouch of dragon milk heals current wounds and eases withdrawal discomfort from tobacco
column3: alcohol and narcotics. If you have Sentinel Collapse
column4: each pouch reduces the days since your last injection by 5
column5: down to a minimum of 0. The milk is also rich in nutrients. The whole pouch is consumed at once.

name: manual_dairy_note_11_section_2
Sarrona: Using ambergris before opening

name: manual_dairy_note_11_body_2
Sarrona: Using one dose of Dragon Ambergris raises selling prices by 10% for the day. The effect wears off the following day. If another perfume is used too
column3: the stronger selling bonus applies. Any discount that perfume gives when buying goods still applies.

name: manual_print_note_12_title
Sarrona: Fitting and Using Attachments

name: manual_print_note_12_section_1
Sarrona: Springs and sights

name: manual_print_note_12_body_1
Sarrona: Dragon-Bone Precision Springs share the internal spring slot. Remove the existing springs before fitting them. The Dragon-Bone Sight fits the red-dot sight slot. Springs improve reliability
column3: while the sight improves accuracy and style.

name: manual_print_note_12_section_2
Sarrona: Suppressors and extended magazines

name: manual_print_note_12_body_2
Sarrona: The Dragon-Bone Suppressor improves recoil control
column3: while the extended magazine improves firepower. Both improve style and reduce ergonomics. Purer bone bricks give greater bonuses to reliability
column4: accuracy
column5: recoil control or firepower.

name: manual_print_note_12_section_3
Sarrona: Compatibility and storage

name: manual_print_note_12_body_3
Sarrona: The extended magazine fits the printed gun and handmade pistol as well as the Fire Dragon Lin. The suppressor and extended magazine need extra space. Inspect each attachment to view its stats.

Once mixed, its rich milky flavor masks the taste of less-than-pure water. It can also give the immune system a modest boost and help wounds heal. name: milk_can_food_flavor

Some of the flavor and nutritional value are lost, but the powder is still a rare source of concentrated energy. And that loss is deliberate on Sarrona's part. People in the upper district taste it and say it falls short of the original. It gives them one more way to mark the difference between classes, so they don't bother making trouble over a few tins.

name: manual_dairy_note_12_title
Sarrona: Large batches and dry storage

name: manual_dairy_note_12_section_1
Sarrona: Drying module

name: manual_dairy_note_12_body_1
Sarrona: Heat the milk to at least 100°C to sterilize it. A standard evaporator with one drying module handles 5 L a night and uses 96 power. Extra modules speed it up and draw more power. If you thin the concentrate with water, give it time to evaporate. If you add fresh milk, sterilize the batch again.

name: manual_dairy_note_12_section_2
Sarrona: Storage and sale

name: manual_dairy_note_12_body_2
Sarrona: Dry powder keeps well. Set some aside loose for nutrient tablets, or seal it in cans to sell as food. Every 80 mL of pure milk powder is worth 20 credits. A full can is valued by how much powder it holds, plus the price of the empty tin. When canning, the machine takes only the milk powder and leaves the residue in the bottle. When pressing tablets, the residue goes into the tablets. Sarrona refuses her own milk powder.

name: manual_dairy_note_13_title
Sarrona: Printed cans and batch filling

name: manual_dairy_note_13_section_1
Sarrona: Preparing cans

name: manual_dairy_note_13_body_1
Sarrona: Every 500 mL of fresh milk yields 200 mL of dry powder. Switch the Bottle Printer to cans. Small cans hold 450 mL and cost 4 power to print. Standard cans hold 750 mL (6 power) and large cans hold 2 L (11 power). Each size unlocks with its matching bottle.

name: manual_dairy_note_13_section_2
Sarrona: Batch filling

name: manual_dairy_note_13_body_2
Sarrona: Put the dry powder container in the Chem Finisher input and empty cans in the output. Select “Can Wild Dragon Milk Powder” and press Produce. The machine fills each can to capacity and crimps it shut. If there is too little powder for a large can, a smaller one may still fit the batch. Excess powder stays in the input.

name: manual_print_note_13_title
Sarrona: Bottle Printer and printed cans

name: manual_print_note_13_section_1
Sarrona: Printing cans

name: manual_print_note_13_body_1
Sarrona: The Bottle Printer can switch between bottles and cans. Small, standard and large cans hold 450 mL, 750 mL and 2 L, costing 4, 6 and 11 power per print. Upgrading unlocks standard and large cans alongside their bottles. This machine prints them directly; no Metal Printing Module or dragon-bone chip is needed.

name: manual_print_note_13_section_2
Sarrona: Filling and sealing

name: manual_print_note_13_body_2
Sarrona: These cans are made for the Chem Finisher. Place the dry powder container in the input and empty cans in the output. Select the canning recipe and press Produce. Each can is filled to capacity and sealed permanently. Set aside any loose powder you want to press into tablets before canning.
